title: Invisible to humans, visible to machines: a preregistered audit of Unicode fidelity across four biomedical bibliographic APIs
abstract: arXiv:2606.24897v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: To develop a reusable, preregistered method for auditing the character-level fidelity of bibliographic application programming interfaces (APIs), and to apply it to four public APIs used to build biomedical text corpora. Preregistered audit (OSF osf.io/zjevr). From the 2024 PubMed Central (PMC) Open Access subset, a simple random sample of 4,000 English-language research articles was drawn. Abstracts returned by the PubMed E-utilities, Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were compared with the PMC Journal Article Tag Suite (JATS) XML abstract for 51 registered code points, 34 of them in four primary classes: typographic punctuation, mathematical/scientific symbols, Greek letters and special whitespace. A cell (API x class) was classified as systematic loss when the upper 95% Wilson bound of conditional preservation was below 5%, and as faithful when the lower bound exceeded 90%. translated_title: 对人类不可见，对机器可见：四项生物医学文献API的Unicode保真度预注册审计
translated_abstract: 本研究旨在开发一种可复用、预注册的方法，用于审计文献应用程序编程接口（API）的字符级保真度，并将其应用于用于构建生物医学文本语料库的四个公共API。这是一项预注册审计（OSF osf.io/zjevr）。研究从2024年PubMed Central（PMC）开放获取子集中简单随机抽取了4000篇英文研究论文，将PubMed E-utilities、Crossref、OpenAlex和Semantic Scholar返回的摘要与PMC期刊文章标签套件（JATS）XML摘要进行对比，共涉及51个注册码点，其中34个属于四个主要类别：排版标点符号、数学/科学符号、希腊字母和特殊空白字符。当条件保留率的95% Wilson置信区间上限低于5%时，某单元格（API x 类别）被归类为系统性丢失；当置信区间下限超过90%时，则被归类为保真。研究还对每类丢失的机制进行了检验……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究开发并预注册了一种可复用的字符级保真度审计方法，系统评估了PubMed、Crossref、OpenAlex和Semantic Scholar四个生物医学文献API对Unicode特殊字符（如希腊字母、数学符号、排版标点和特殊空白）的保留能力，揭示了这些API存在的系统性字符丢失问题。
en_tdlr: This study developed and preregistered a reusable method for auditing character-level fidelity, systematically evaluating how four biomedical bibliographic APIs (PubMed, Crossref, OpenAlex, and Semantic Scholar) preserve Unicode special characters such as Greek letters, mathematical symbols, typographic punctuation, and special whitespace, thereby revealing systematic character loss in these APIs.
